digest.component_or_area: RP-04 secrets and authentication architecture research
propositions: Rebar must delegate authentication to provider-native SDKs and credential helpers rather than implementing a universal secret broker or credential store.
Static credentials must be materialized only at the adapter boundary that requires them, wrapped in non-serializable containers, and excluded from operation snapshots.

Process-local context binding and per-job credential refresh replace global environment mutation; deployment resolves external secret stores before Rebar startup and supplies credentials via REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY.

Subprocess children inherit ambient trusted environment for compatibility; unrelated sibling processes remove only exact Rebar-declared secret names; native Git/SSH/AWS/proxy credential chains remain intact.
Static credential rotation occurs via restart/redeploy with externally managed replacement visibility; hot-reload polling, file watchers, and cloud-secret manager integration are out of scope.

Provider-specific typed injection seams accept native credential/session/identity capabilities (e.g. boto3 Session, Anthropic AccessTokenProvider) into Rebar-owned factories; arbitrary whole-client injection bypassing Rebar policy is not supported in the initial implementation.
